item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in VS Code, Universe releases
item.description:
GitHub says the 2026 Universe release for Copilot in VS Code adds more choice over which models you use, where agents run, and how you work with Copilot. The provided excerpt does not include the specific feature list.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Repository plugin defaults and enterprise plugin controls generally available
item.description:
Repository plugin defaults and enterprise-managed plugin controls are now generally available for VS Code, Copilot CLI, and the GitHub Copilot app. Trusted repositories can install and enable default plugins, and enterprises can manage plugin controls centrally.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: vscode: VS Code Wrapped: GitHub Universe 2026
item.description:
The article says VS Code evolved from GitHub Universe 2025 to 2026, focusing on new coding workflows, collaboration with agents, and managing work across tools and environments. The provided text is a brief overview and does not include specific feature details.

  • Source: VS Code Updates and Blog

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot assisted permissions generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot assisted permissions are now generally available in Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, and Visual Studio Code. The feature lets Copilot request permission before running commands or accessing file system paths.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: vscode: Tune GitHub Copilot Inline Suggestions with Configurable Eagerness
item.description:
The article announces a new setting to control how proactively GitHub Copilot shows inline suggestions in VS Code. It lets users tune suggestion eagerness rather than using a fixed behavior.

  • Source: VS Code Updates and Blog

item.title: vscode: Modernizing the VS Code UI
item.description:
The article says VS Code’s interface is being updated based on developer feedback, with changes focused on layout density, editor tabs, themes, and responsiveness. It points readers to the full post for details.

  • Source: VS Code Updates and Blog

item.title: github: HydraFusion updates and new Max option
item.description:
HydraFusion now has an updated model pool and improved orchestration workflows. A new HydraFusion Max option is also available, with both offerings supported in VS Code, the GitHub Copilot app, and GitHub Copilot.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Local sandboxing for GitHub Copilot now generally available
item.description:
Local sandboxing for GitHub Copilot is now generally available. It is supported in GitHub Copilot CLI, the GitHub Copilot app, and VS Code sessions using Agent Host.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in VS Code, September 2026 releases
item.description:
September 2026 GitHub Copilot in VS Code releases cover VS Code v1.136 through v1.140 and focus on streamlining agent-driven development from implementation through pull request merge. The update adds automations for repeatable tasks and agent merge support.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — September 21
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s weekly release roundup adds new models, local sandboxing in the Copilot app, and updates across Copilot integrations in Slack, Microsoft Teams, JetBrains, and VS Code.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Introducing a Guided Copilot Experience for Building Azure Apps in VS Code
item.description:
Microsoft is previewing a guided Copilot experience in VS Code for building Azure apps. It provides a structured workflow that helps move from idea to deployed app instead of relying on a free-form chat session.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: ai: Introducing Foundry Dev Pack: One Command to Start Building
item.description:
Microsoft announced Foundry Dev Pack, an all-in-one installer that prepares a machine for Microsoft Foundry development. It installs the tools needed for use in the terminal, VS Code, and coding agents.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: github: Add VS Code Agents to Copilot usage metrics
item.description:
GitHub Copilot usage metrics now include generally available activity metrics for the dedicated VS Code Agents window. This lets enterprises and organizations track adoption and engagement for VS Code Agents alongside other Copilot usage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — August 31
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s latest weekly release adds more model choice and content protection controls. VS Code also gets new options for managing agent sessions and preparing pull requests for merge.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in VS Code, August 2026 releases
item.description:
VS Code v1.132 through v1.135, released in August 2026, add improvements to GitHub Copilot workflows focused on organizing agent sessions, reviewing changes, and navigating longer conversations. The changelog also mentions updates to Agent Host, but the provided excerpt does not include the details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Agent Plugins 1.0 in VS Code, Copilot CLI, and the Copilot app
item.description:
GitHub published Agent Plugins 1.0, enabling a plugin to be built once and used across compatible agent clients. The release is available in VS Code, Copilot CLI, and the Copilot app, with support announced alongside AWS, Anysphere, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Vercel.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — August 3
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s August 3 weekly release notes mention updates across the desktop app, CLI, and VS Code focused on resuming and organizing work, reviewing changes, and asking questions without losing context. The provided excerpt does not include the specific feature details.

  • Source: GitHub
